title: Slices of 2D cellular automata resemble 1D cellular automata

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Slices of 2D cellular automata resemble 1D cellular automata

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The complexity inside patterns generated by two-dimensional totalistic cellular automata is very similar to that of one-dimensional cellular automata: a one-dimensional slice through the 2D pattern evolves much like an ordinary 1D cellular automaton.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: if one looks at the evolution of a one-dimensional slice through each two-dimensional pattern the results one gets are strikingly similar to what we have seen in ordinary one-dimensional cellular automata.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 5, “Two Dimensions and Beyond”; section “Cellular Automata” (from p. 170), p. 176. Scope: two-dimensional outer totalistic cellular automata from a single seed

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch05-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.76

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The prescribed outputs and slices are straightforward to compute, and comparisons can be preregistered. Broad similarity remains metric- and sample-dependent, so current resources resolve representative cases rather than the unrestricted class.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Generate two-dimensional outer-totalistic automata from single seeds, extract fixed one-dimensional slices over time, and compare their spatiotemporal statistics and predictive features with matched one-dimensional automata. Quantified similarity or separability resolves the claim for sampled rules.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Strikingly similar requires a chosen metric.

Available catalogs do not cover every rule and slice choice.

Slices of a 2D system need not obey a closed 1D local rule.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.65
discriminating power: 0.7
data existence: 0.88
operationalizability: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.84

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The objects compared are explicit evolutions, and both the two-dimensional rules and the one-dimensional comparison class are standard to simulate. A predeclared similarity measure on a large totalistic sample would confirm or strain the visual claim. Without a sharp cutoff for 'very similar,' the exercise remains a partial, informative test rather than a yes-or-no resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Evolve two-dimensional totalistic cellular automata from a single seed, extract the central one-dimensional slice, and score that slice with a classifier trained on ordinary one-dimensional cellular automata. Systematic mismatch of behavior types would challenge 'strikingly similar'; agreement on a large rule sample would support it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Similarity of pictures can be strong while a quantitative classifier still disagrees, or the reverse.

The slice through the middle is one observable; other slices can look less like one-dimensional cellular automata.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.7
discriminating power: 0.55
data existence: 0.85
analysis feasibility: 0.8
operationalizability: 0.7
